item.title: Accused of sexual abuse in Spain and Bolivia, Jesuit priest escapes trial due to statute of limitations
item.description: Jesuit Father Francesc Peris, accused by numerous former students of committing sexual abuse against them at a school in Barcelona, Spain, and another in Cochabamba, Bolivia, will not face criminal prosecution.

item.title: Pope urges men, women to be witnesses of fraternity in divided world
item.description: Pope Leo celebrated the service of consecrated men and women Monday, telling those who had given their lives to God that they are meant to be witnesses of peace and fraternity in a divided and conflicted world.

item.title: Catholic Church and Italy investigate sacred and profane cherub seemingly modeled on Meloni
item.description: There is a long tradition of painters depicting real people in their religious art, but the appearance in a Roman church of a cherub that bears a striking resemblance to Premier Giorgia Meloni has sparked a minor scandal.

item.title: Trevi Fountain fee goes into effect as Rome seeks to manage tourist flow at celebrated water feature
item.description: Tourists hoping to get close to the Trevi Fountain had to pay 2 euros ($2.35) starting Monday as the city of Rome inaugurated a new fee structure to help raise money and control crowds at the one of the world’s most celebrated waterworks.

item.title: Nine arraigned for deadly attack in Nigeria that killed over 150
item.description: Nine people accused of carrying out a deadly attack in north-central Nigeria were arraigned before a federal court on Monday, charged in connection with the deaths of more than 150 people.

item.title: From southern India to Canada’s far north: New archbishop serves Indigenous Catholics
item.description: As a teenager in southern India, Susai Jesu led 4:30 a.m. prayer services in his small Catholic village before the farmers went into the fields. He directed the choir, helped at Mass and soon began training for the priesthood.

item.title: Michelangelo’s ‘The Last Judgment’ fresco undergoes 3-month cleaning at Sistine Chapel
item.description: Michelangelo’s “The Last Judgment,” the imposing fresco of heaven and hell which dominates the Sistine Chapel, is undergoing its first major restoration in three decades, the Vatican said Monday.

item.title: Pope Leo and the meaning of ‘manners’
item.description: Anyone who has ever been in a serious relationship will probably identify with the old and by now cliché adage, “it’s not what you said, it’s how you said it” at the end of some form of disagreement.

item.title: Vatican’s ‘trial of the century’ resumes after prosecutors suffer embarrassing setbacks on appeal
item.description: The appeals phase of the Vatican’s “trial of the century” resumed Tuesday after a pair of setbacks for the pope’s prosecutors that could have big repercussions on the outcome of the troubled case.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV faces crisis as a traditionalist group plans bishop consecrations without consent
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is facing his first major crisis with traditionalist Catholics, after a breakaway group attached to the traditional Latin Mass announced plans to consecrate new bishops without papal consent in a threatened revival of schism.
